# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 24 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Thanksgiving Hymns Column 24 where the three translators significantly diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 24:4 — "son of Adam" vs. "human being" — anthropological formula

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-son-of Adam" | Literal ben 'adam with article |
| LOGOS | "a son of Adam" | Hebraic idiom preserved |
| PNEUMA | "a human being" | Modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Son of Adam" is the standard Hodayot self-abasement term connecting humanity to its earthly origin. PNEUMA's "human being" loses the Adamic resonance.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:7 — "dwelling" vs. "abode" vs. "home" — register for human habitation among worms

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his dwelling is with worms" | Literal megurah |
| LOGOS | "his abode is among the worms" | Formal register; "among" for spatial sense |
| PNEUMA | "our home is among the worms" | Shift to first-person plural; "home" is colloquial |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Abode" has the appropriate archaic-formal register for the passage. PNEUMA's shift to first-person plural is unwarranted by the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:8 — "pinched off" — potter imagery

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "pinched-off" | Literal qerets — pottery term for shaping clay |
| LOGOS | "a thing pinched off" | Expanded with nominal phrase |
| PNEUMA | "molded and pinched off" | Added "molded" for contextual clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "A thing pinched off" gives the pottery term an English frame while preserving the vivid metaphor. PNEUMA's "molded" is redundant with the preceding clay imagery.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:16 — "sons of Your truth" vs. "children of Your truth" vs. "all who belong to Your truth"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-sons-of Your truth" | Literal bene 'amittekha |
| LOGOS | "the children of Your truth" | "Children" as gender-inclusive alternative to "sons" |
| PNEUMA | "all who belong to Your truth" | Paraphrastic expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Children of Your truth" preserves the familial metaphor while being more inclusive. PNEUMA's expansion loses the kinship language.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:17 — "forgiveness" vs. "pardon" vs. "forgiveness" — term for divine absolution

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "into forgiveness" | Standard selichah |
| LOGOS | "into pardon" | "Pardon" carries legal-covenantal overtones |
| PNEUMA | "into forgiveness" | Same as EMET |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Pardon" better reflects the forensic-covenantal context of the Hodayot where the relationship between God and the community is structured legally.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:27 — "doers of wickedness" vs. "evildoers" vs. "everyone who does evil"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-doers-of wickedness" | Literal po'alei 'avlah |
| LOGOS | "all evildoers" | Concise single-word equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "everyone who does evil" | Expanded relative clause |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. "Evildoers" is concise and immediately comprehensible. EMET's construction is awkward; PNEUMA's expansion is wordy.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
